## Your two-afternoon route

Work in pairs, but keep your own code and explanations. You do not need prior R experience.

[Download the complete student project](statistics_lab_student.zip). Extract it and open `Statistics_lab.Rproj`. Keep the folder together.

### Before class

[Setup and launch instructions](notebooks/00_setup.html). Install and test the tutorial before the first afternoon.

### Day 1 — a molecule, a mouse, and a memory

Use the live **learnr** tutorial: short code editors, feedback, interactive plots and answer boxes. In the project's RStudio Console run:

```r
source("scripts/run_day1.R")
```

[Read the day-1 preview](day1_preview.html). This is a static reading copy, not the live exercise. Download your practice Rmd before closing the live tutorial.

### Day 2 — your MMSE investigation

Open [02_mmse_investigation.Rmd](notebooks/02_mmse_investigation.Rmd) **in RStudio** and save your own copy. You will investigate human cognition using the same summaries, plots and statistical reasoning as yesterday.

[Read the task preview](notebooks/02_mmse_investigation.html) · [R Notebook snapshot](notebooks/02_mmse_investigation.nb.html) · [Command reference](notebooks/03_command_reference.html)

Submit one freshly knitted **HTML report** per student with your code, figures and own explanations. Keep your `.Rmd` source. The supplied preview is a draft with no student conclusions.

### What you will be able to explain

What one observation means; how variable type affects summaries; mean, median, SD, quartiles and IQR; the information in distributions and plots; why a test fits a question; effect and uncertainty; association versus causation; and why multiple testing matters.

[Data dictionary and provenance](data/dictionary.html). Day 1 uses 72 mice; day 2 uses one first visit from each of 136 people. These are separate datasets, not measurements to combine.
